title: Agent tree
description: Coding agents as a process tree, with the rules Linux uses: every agent has a pid, a parent and exactly one state (working, waiting, needs you, paused, done, or failed with an exit code), shown by a mark and named beside the pid; needs you stands out as an inverted pill; you are process 1 at the top. Selecting an agent shows its reach: what it steers (everything below it and the lines down to it, in the one colour); its own row takes a quiet tint. Sockets between siblings, opened by a shared ancestor, and two agents in one file show on the rows, naming the other agents. On a phone a row keeps the task and drops the pid and letter. Keyboard: arrows move, Enter selects. An `actions` snippet renders the app's own actions on the right of the selected row, so selecting moves nothing; render none where none apply (a finished agent).
